title: Optimize Console — Apply Concierge: staged cards, diff preview, and action history inspector
creator: Asha Patel
summary: Ship a unified Apply Concierge in Optimize that lets users stage batching/caching recommendations as interactive cards, inspect a side-by-side diff preview of resulting config changes, and view a tamper-evident action history with rollback helpers.
background: Customers run Optimize to get automated batching and KV cache recommendations. Today the console surfaces suggestions as isolated cards and emits an apply event, but teams report low trust: they want to rehearse combined config changes, understand precise diffs across routes/models, and have a clear, auditable trail for who applied what and why. This reduces adoption of automated savings and increases manual ops overhead.
goals: 1) Provide a staging surface where multiple recommendations can be composed into a single apply bundle. 2) Offer a clear, line-level diff preview of config changes (routes, model variants, batch/latency thresholds). 3) Record a cryptographically-stamped action history that shows who staged, reviewed, approved, and applied changes, and provides a one-click safe rollback. 4) Preserve deterministic test replay (dry-run) and link to workload simulations for regression checks.
non_goals: 1) This scope does not include runtime autoscaling engine changes or new batching algorithms. 2) It does not replace enterprise change management (e.g., Jira approvals) but integrates with them via links and webhooks. 3) Not implementing HSM-backed signature in this iteration.
user_stories: As a platform engineer, I want to combine 3 Optimize recommendations into a single staged bundle so I can evaluate them together before applying.
As an SRE, I want a side-by-side diff that highlights per-route token-level impacts and latency projections so I can make safety trade-offs.
As a PM, I want an immutable audit entry showing who approved and applied the change and a quick rollback button that reverts to the previous config.
As a developer, I want to run a dry-run simulation from the Apply Concierge and see expected cost delta and risk signals before committing.
proposed_solution: Introduce an 'Apply Concierge' panel in Optimize. The flow: users select recommendation cards (single or multi-select). Selected recommendations are added to a Staging Rack. From the rack they can reorder, annotate, and toggle recommendations on/off. A ‘Preview Bundle’ opens a diff canvas that shows before/after JSON snippets for affected routes and a summarized token/cost delta heatmap. The action modal captures the actor, optional rationale, and applies at a chosen rollout cadence (immediate, gradual canary percent, scheduled). After apply, an immutable Action Record is created containing the bundle snapshot, diff, rollout parameters, and links to simulation results. The Action Record surfaces a one-click 'Safe Rewind' which enqueues an automated revert that re-applies the previous bundle using the same rollout policy and captures a revert record.
ui_flows: Main listing: recommendation cards with hover actions (Inspect, Add to Staging, Simulate).
Staging Rack: compact horizontal tray anchored at bottom; shows selected cards, order drag handles, and aggregate cost delta badge.
Preview Canvas: left column original config, right column proposed config, inline highlights for changed keys; top bar with summary (tokens saved, estimated latency delta, risk score).
Apply Modal: actor, rationale, rollout options (Immediate / Canary %) and checkbox 'Run dry-run simulation' with link to recent simulation run.
Action Inspector: chronological entries with bundle snapshot, who changed status (staged, reviewed, applied), links to PRs/notes, and Rewind button (disabled if external dependency prevents revert).
data_and_models: Store Bundle as an immutable JSON snapshot in the Optimize ledger with fields: bundle_id, recommendations[], pre_config_hash, post_config_hash, actor, timestamp, rollout_policy, simulation_id. Action Records reference bundle_id and append event transitions (staged->reviewed->applied->reverted). Index by route and model for fast query. Note: actual storage design and size constraints will be handled by infra; here we capture required keys and retention policy (retain 1 year by default, configurable for enterprise).
telemetry_and_metrics: Emit events: bundle_staged, bundle_previewed, bundle_simulated, bundle_applied, bundle_reverted. Track metrics: time_in_staging, percent_of_bundles_with_simulation, median_rollback_time, cost_saved_30d_after_apply, incidence_of_post_apply_regressions. Attach token-level sample traces for 7 days when simulation runs.
rollout_plan: 1) Experimental flag behind onboarding tenant and internal beta. 2) Week 1: internal power users + 3 pilot customers. 3) Week 2: open to all accounts with opt-in. 4) Week 4: GA with default enabled for Optimize customers. Provide migration path for existing single-card apply UX to map to bundling.
ab_testing_and_validation: A/B test: control (current single-card apply) vs treatment (Apply Concierge). Primary outcome: percent_of_recommendations_applied_per_user within 14 days. Secondary: post-apply_regression_rate, mean time to rollback. Validate with 3 pilot tenants before GA.
acceptance_criteria: Users can multi-select recommendation cards and add them to the Staging Rack.
Preview Canvas shows accurate before/after config diffs for routes impacted by the bundle.
Apply Modal records actor and rationale and triggers an apply that updates runtime configs within SLOs.
Action Record is persisted and searchable by bundle_id, route, and actor.
Rewind action reverts to pre-config state in <= 10 minutes for simple reverts and logs a revert Action Record.
Telemetry events for each lifecycle transition emitted and visible in observability dashboards.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Users may stage conflicting recommendations that cause runtime errors. Mitigation: run validation during Preview that detects incompatible key changes and prevents apply.
Risk: Large bundles could cause lengthy rollout windows. Mitigation: enforce default canary and per-route rate limits, and warn on bundles affecting >50 routes.
Risk: Audit tampering. Mitigation: ledger snapshots include content hashes and are append-only; surface signature proof for enterprise in subsequent iteration.
dependencies: ENG-33344 (Simulation service: dry-run runner and telemetry export)
open_questions: Should reverting create a new bundle that explicitly reverses diffs or simply restore the pre_config snapshot?
What retention policy and export format do compliance customers require for Action Records beyond the default 1 year?
Do we need an approval step in the first GA for enterprise orgs (SSO group gating)?
